## BUDGET (continued): Ballpark Totals

*Excludes rent, security deposits, and temporary housing, which depend on your new place.*

| Scenario | Estimated Total |
|---|---|
| **DIY truck**, you drive the truck + car | **$3,000–$6,500** |
| **Portable container**, you drive the car | **$3,500–$7,000** |
| **Hybrid** (you pack, movers load/drive) | **$4,000–$7,500** |
| **Full-service movers**, you drive the car | **$6,200–$12,500** |
| Add: ship one car (open carrier) | +$900–$1,400 |
| Add: ship one car (enclosed) | +$1,600–$2,300 |
| Add: temporary housing (1–2 wks) | +$800–$2,000 |
| Add: 10–15% contingency | Recommended for all |

**Tips:**
- **Mid-month and weekday moves** are often cheaper. July is peak season, so book soon.
- If you have **two cars**, both of you driving one is usually cheaper than shipping, but it means no co-driver relief and the dog rides with one person.
- **Towing a car behind a DIY truck** (car trailer ~$300–$600) is an option if only one of you can drive a truck.

# Room-by-Room Packing Plan + Declutter Guide

**Built around your move day: Thursday, July 16, 2026.** Time estimates assume a 1–2 bedroom home with two people working together. **Rule of thumb: everything takes 1.5× longer than you think**, so the schedule has buffer built in.

**Total estimated time: ~45–75 hours** across 5 weeks (≈ 10–15 hrs/week).

---

## 🗓️ THE ORDER (and Why)

Pack from **least-used to most-used.** Kitchen, bathrooms, and bedrooms go last.

| # | Area | Target Dates | Est. Time | Who |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Storage unit** (if any) | Jun 13–14 | 4–8 hrs | J |
| 2 | **Garage / shed / attic** | Jun 20–28 | 6–12 hrs | J |
| 3 | **Spare room + hall/storage closets** | Jun 25–28 | 3–5 hrs | P |
| 4 | **Books, decor, art, off-season clothes** | Jun 27–Jul 2 | 3–6 hrs | M |
| 5 | **Living room** | Jul 3–8 (use July 4 weekend) | 4–6 hrs | J |
| 6 | **Dining room** | Jul 3–8 | 2–3 hrs | P |
| 7 | **Home office** | Jul 6–10 (work gear last) | 3–5 hrs | Owner of the gear |
| 8 | **Kitchen** (80% packed) | Jul 8–13 | 8–12 hrs | J |
| 9 | **Bathrooms** | Jul 12–14 | 1–2 hrs each | M |
| 10 | **Bedrooms + closets** | Jul 12–15 | 6–10 hrs | J |
| 11 | **Dog gear + Open First box + car kit** | Jul 15 | 1–2 hrs | M |

---

## ✂️ DECLUTTER PHASE: Jun 11–24 (Do This *Before* Packing)

Do one fast sorting pass through every room with four bins or piles: **KEEP · SELL · DONATE · TRASH.**

**The Cross-Country Decision Rule**
Long-distance moves are priced largely by **weight**, often roughly $0.50–$1+ per pound with full-service movers. Get rid of an item if **2 or more** of these are true:
- [ ] You haven't used it in 12 months
- [ ] Replacing it in Oregon would cost less than moving it
- [ ] It's particle-board or flat-pack furniture (it often doesn't survive a move)
- [ ] It won't fit or suit the new place (measure first!)
- [ ] You're keeping it "just in case"

**Where Things Go**

| Item Type | Best Outlet | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Furniture, appliances, electronics | Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist, OfferUp, Nextdoor | **List by Jun 14**; final sale cutoff **Jul 10** |
| Furniture/building materials (donate) | Habitat ReStore (free pickup), Salvation Army | **Book pickup 2–3 wks ahead** |
| Clothes, housewares, books | Goodwill, local thrift, library book sales | Drop off weekly |
| Anything (fast and free) | Buy Nothing groups, curbside "free" post | Anytime |
| Old towels, blankets, sheets | **Animal shelters** (they love these) | Anytime |
| Unopened pantry food | Food pantries | Week 2 |
| Paint, chemicals, batteries, e-waste | **County household hazardous waste drop-off** | Check hours early |
| Documents you don't need | Shred event or office store shredding | Week 3 |

**Declutter Tips**
- **Price to sell, not to profit.** Price 30–50% below market. Unsold items cost you money to move or haul away.
- **Sell big items first.** Pick up any replacements in Oregon.
- **Set a hard "last donation run" date (Jul 11).** Anything left goes to the curb or junk removal.
- **Measure the new place** (rooms, doorways, stairs) before deciding on large furniture.
- **Don't pack trash.** Toss expired food, meds, makeup, broken items, and orphan cables as you go.

---

## 🏷️ LABELING SYSTEM

**1. Color-code each room with colored tape or stickers**

| Room | Color |
|---|---|
| Kitchen | 🔴 Red |
| Living / Dining | 🟠 Orange |
| Primary Bedroom | 🔵 Blue |
| Spare / Office | 🟢 Green |
| Bathroom | 🟣 Purple |
| Garage / Tools | ⚫ Black |
| Dog | 🟡 Yellow |

**2. Write this format on the top and 2 sides of every box**

```
KIT-14  |  P1  |  Coffee maker, mugs, filters  |  FRAGILE ↑
```
- **Room code + number** (KIT, LIV, BED, OFF, BATH, GAR, DOG)
- **Priority:** **P1** = open first day · **P2** = first week · **P3** = whenever
- **Short contents** plus **FRAGILE** and **↑ THIS SIDE UP** where needed

**3. Keep a shared box inventory** in a Google Sheet or Notes app with columns for **Box # · Room · Contents · Priority · Fragile?** Snap a photo of each open box before sealing.
→ At delivery, **check off box numbers** to confirm nothing's missing. This matters if you need to file a claim.

**4. At the new house:** tape a matching color square on each room's door so movers (or you) know where boxes go.

---

## 🧰 SUPPLIES (Buy by Jun 20)

| Item | Qty (1–2 BR) |
|---|---|
| Small boxes (books, heavy items) | 20–25 |
| Medium boxes (most stuff) | 25–30 |
| Large boxes (light, bulky items only) | 10–15 |
| Wardrobe boxes | 3–5 |
| Dish-pack boxes (double-wall) with cell dividers | 2–4 |
| TV box kit (if no original box) | 1 per TV |
| Mirror/picture boxes + corner protectors | As needed |
| Packing tape | 6–10 rolls |
| Packing paper (plain newsprint) | 20–25 lbs |
| Bubble wrap | 1–2 large rolls |
| Stretch wrap (furniture/drawers) | 1–2 rolls |
| Mattress bags | 1 per mattress |
| Markers, colored tape, zip bags (hardware) | 1 pack each |

---

## 🥚 FRAGILE PACKING RULES

**General**
- [ ] **Max ~50 lbs per box.** Heavy items go in **small** boxes, light items in large ones.
- [ ] Crumpled paper on the **bottom and top**. **No empty space.** If the box rattles, add more fill.
- [ ] Use **plain packing paper, not newspaper** (ink transfers onto dishes).
- [ ] Tape the bottom with an **"H" pattern**.

**Dishes and Glassware**
- [ ] **Plates:** wrap individually, stand them **on edge like records**, never flat.
- [ ] **Glasses and stemware:** wrap, stuff the inside with paper, use cell dividers, and put them **rim-down**.
- [ ] **Bowls:** nest 2–3 with paper between them, wrapped together.
- [ ] Heaviest items on the bottom, lightest on top.

**Electronics**
- [ ] **Photograph the cable setup** before unplugging. Bag and label cords together.
- [ ] Use original boxes if you have them. Otherwise, wrap in an anti-static or bubble layer.
- [ ] **TVs travel upright**, never flat.
- [ ] **Laptops, hard drives, and cameras go in the car, not the truck.**

**Art, Mirrors, Glass**
- [ ] Tape a large **"X" across glass** to hold shards if it cracks.
- [ ] Add corner protectors and bubble wrap, then use a mirror/picture box.
- [ ] Mark **"FRAGILE: DO NOT LAY FLAT"** and transport upright.

**Lamps and Odd Shapes**
- [ ] Remove bulbs and shades. Pack shades separately, nested if possible, with no heavy items on top.
- [ ] Wrap the base in bubble wrap.

**Furniture**
- [ ] Remove legs and hardware. Put screws in a **labeled zip bag taped to the furniture**.
- [ ] Stretch-wrap drawers shut (don't tape directly on wood finishes).
- [ ] Photograph furniture condition for insurance.

---

## 🏠 ROOM-BY-ROOM CHECKLISTS

### 1. 🏬 STORAGE UNIT (Jun 13–14 · 4–8 hrs · J)
*Goal: empty it early and stop paying rent on it.*
- [ ] Check your contract's move-out notice (often 10–30 days). **Give notice now.**
- [ ] Sort on-site: KEEP / SELL / DONATE / TRASH. Bring bins and trash bags.
- [ ] Book a truck or van, or ask a friend with a pickup.
- [ ] Consolidate keepers into the garage or a spare room.
- [ ] Check for items affected by heat or moisture (electronics, documents, mildew).
- [ ] Sweep out, remove your lock, and **get written move-out confirmation**.
- [ ] Cancel autopay and confirm the deposit refund.

### 2. 🔧 GARAGE / SHED / ATTIC (Jun 20–28 · 6–12 hrs · J)
*Usually the most time-consuming area to sort, so don't leave it late.*

**⚠️ Movers will NOT transport these.** Plan to use up, give away, or properly dispose of them:
- [ ] Gasoline, propane tanks, lighter fluid, kerosene
- [ ] Paint, stains, solvents, aerosols
- [ ] Pool or cleaning chemicals, fertilizer, pesticides
- [ ] Ammunition, fireworks
- [ ] Car batteries; loose lithium batteries (tape the terminals and keep them with you)
- [ ] **Firewood: don't move it.** It can spread invasive pests like the emerald ash borer.

**Checklist**
- [ ] **Drain gas and oil** from mowers, trimmers, and other gas tools (required by most movers).
- [ ] Donate duplicate tools and cleaning supplies, or leave them for the next occupant if allowed.
- [ ] Sell bulky items you won't need (snowblower? Depends where in Oregon you're going).
- [ ] Clean and dry outdoor gear, bikes, and coolers.
- [ ] Bundle long-handled tools with tape or stretch wrap.
- [ ] Pack small tools in small, heavy-duty boxes. Bag hardware by type.
- [ ] Set aside a **"Moving Toolkit"** for the car: drill, screwdrivers, Allen keys, tape measure, utility knife, hammer.
- [ ] Attic: check for forgotten boxes, holiday decor, and anything stored in eaves.
- [ ] **Plants:** Oregon has agricultural quarantine rules, and Ohio is in the Japanese beetle range. **Check Oregon Department of Agriculture guidance** before moving potted plants or soil. Gifting them is often easiest.

### 3. 🛏️ SPARE ROOM + STORAGE CLOSETS (Jun 25–28 · 3–5 hrs · P)
- [ ] Pack guest bedding, keeping one set out for the trip if needed.
- [ ] Hobby and craft supplies, luggage you won't use, and keepsakes.
- [ ] Holiday decorations (P3).
- [ ] Hall closet: extra linens, coats you won't need in July.
- [ ] **Donate:** duplicate linens, unused gifts, old electronics.

### 4. 📚 BOOKS, DECOR, ART, OFF-SEASON (Jun 27–Jul 2 · 3–6 hrs · M)
- [ ] Books in **small boxes only** (they get heavy fast). Pack them flat or spine-down.
- [ ] Take down art and mirrors. Pack using the fragile rules above.
- [ ] Bag wall hardware. Patch holes now if your lease requires it.
- [ ] Off-season clothes: winter coats, boots, sweaters. Vacuum bags save space.
- [ ] **Declutter:** books you won't reread (library donation), decor that won't fit the new space.

### 5. 🛋️ LIVING ROOM (Jul 3–8 · 4–6 hrs · J)
- [ ] Photograph the TV and media cable setup, then pack electronics.
- [ ] Throw pillows and blankets: use them as padding in other boxes.
- [ ] Remove furniture legs and bag the hardware.
- [ ] Games, media, and remotes (batteries out).
- [ ] Rugs: vacuum, roll, and wrap.
- [ ] **Keep out:** the dog's bed and a couple of seating options until the last 2 days.
- [ ] **Sell:** furniture that won't fit, extra side tables, worn-out pieces.

### 6. 🍽️ DINING ROOM (Jul 3–8 · 2–3 hrs · P)
- [ ] China, serving pieces, and special-occasion glassware go in dish packs.
- [ ] Table leaves wrapped in blankets. Remove the table legs.
- [ ] Linens and placemats.
- [ ] **Declutter:** rarely used serving pieces and duplicate platters.

### 7. 💻 HOME OFFICE (Jul 6–10 · 3–5 hrs · whoever owns the gear)
- [ ] Shred old documents, scan important ones, and back up computers to the cloud **and** an external drive.
- [ ] Pack supplies and reference materials (P3).
- [ ] **Important documents go in the car folder, not a box.**
- [ ] Pack work equipment **last**. Laptops, monitors if possible, and chargers ride with you.
- [ ] Return any employer-owned equipment you won't need, or confirm shipping instructions.
- [ ] **Declutter:** old cables, dead electronics (e-waste), expired paperwork.

### 8. 🍳 KITCHEN (Jul 8–13 · 8–12 hrs · J)
*The most time-intensive room. Split it across several days.*

**Days 1–2 (Jul 8–9): Rarely used items**
- [ ] Specialty appliances (stand mixer, slow cooker, waffle maker).
- [ ] Bakeware, extra pots and pans, serving dishes.
- [ ] Extra glassware and mugs, keeping 2 each out.

**Days 3–4 (Jul 10–11): Most of the rest**
- [ ] Dishes in dish packs, using the fragile rules.
- [ ] Utensils, wrapped together in bundles.
- [ ] Knives: wrap blades in cardboard and tape, then label the bundle **"KNIVES"**.
- [ ] Pantry: **use up, don't move.** Donate unopened food. Movers often won't take perishables, opened liquids, or anything that could leak.

**Day 5 (Jul 12–13): Survival kit only**
- [ ] Keep out 1 pan, 1 pot, 2 plates, 2 bowls, 2 mugs, utensils, a knife, a cutting board, the coffee setup, dish soap, a sponge, and paper towels.
- [ ] **Jul 14:** defrost and clean the fridge and freezer.
- [ ] Survival kit gets packed into the **Open First box** on Jul 15.

**Declutter:** expired spices, duplicate gadgets, mismatched containers, chipped dishes.

### 9. 🛁 BATHROOMS (Jul 12–14 · 1–2 hrs each · M)
- [ ] Toss expired meds, makeup, and near-empty bottles.
- [ ] Tape caps or seal liquids in zip bags. Pack them **upright**.
- [ ] Extra towels can double as padding.
- [ ] **Keep out:** toiletries for the trip, 1 towel each, a shower curtain and rings (into the Open First box), toilet paper, and all **prescriptions (

### 9. 🛁 BATHROOMS (Jul 12–14 · M)

**⏱️ Time per bathroom:**
| Bathroom Type | Est. Time |
|---|---|
| Half bath / powder room | 30–45 min |
| Guest / secondary full bath | 1–1.5 hrs |

**Jul 12: Declutter + pack extras**
- [ ] Toss expired meds, makeup, sunscreen, and near-empty bottles.
- [ ] **Dispose of old medications** at a pharmacy take-back kiosk or police station drop box. Don't flush them.
- [ ] Pack backstock (extra shampoo, soap, cleaning supplies) in **small boxes**, liquids upright.
- [ ] Unscrew caps, add plastic wrap over the opening, screw caps back on, then **zip-bag every liquid**.

- [ ] Hair tools (dryer, straightener) once cool, with cords wrapped.
- [ ] Medicine cabinet items you won't need for the trip.

- [ ] Toiletry bag for each person for 3–4 days on the road.
- [ ] Into the **Open First box:** shower curtain + rings, 1 towel each, toilet paper, hand soap, plunger (seriously), and a small cleaning kit.
- [ ] Wipe down the bathroom for move-out inspection.

**Declutter tips:** Free hotel toiletries, duplicate products, old towels (donate to animal shelters), and anything you'd toss within a month anyway.

---

### 💊 PRESCRIPTION REMINDER: KEEP WITH YOU, NEVER IN THE TRUCK

> **⚠️ All prescriptions (yours, your partner's, and the dog's) ride in the car, in your personal bag, within reach.**

- [ ] **~Jul 1:** Refill all prescriptions so you have **at least a 30-day supply** on move day. Ask your insurer about an early "vacation override" if needed.
- [ ] Keep meds in **original labeled bottles** (helps at pharmacies and if you're stopped or questioned).
- [ ] Pack a **written list** of each med: name, dose, prescriber, pharmacy phone number.
- [ ] **Heat-sensitive meds** (insulin, some liquids, some inhalers) go in a small insulated cooler. Don't leave them in a parked car in July.
- [ ] Include the **dog's meds** in the dog kit, not the moving boxes.
- [ ] **Post-move:** transfer prescriptions to an Oregon pharmacy, and line up new prescribers before your supply runs low.

---

### 10. 🛏️ BEDROOMS + CLOSETS (Jul 12–15 · 6–10 hrs · J)

**⏱️ Time:** Primary bedroom + closet 4–6 hrs · Secondary bedroom 2–4 hrs

- [ ] **Jul 12:** Pack out-of-season and rarely worn clothes. Use **wardrobe boxes** for hanging clothes (move them straight from rod to box).
- [ ] Shoes in their own boxes or bags, stuffed with socks.
- [ ] Jewelry and valuables go **in the car** with documents.
- [ ] **Jul 13–14:** Pack nightstands, dresser contents (light items can stay in drawers if movers allow; stretch-wrap them shut).
- [ ] Keep out **3–4 days of clothes** per person for the road.
- [ ] **Jul 15 (last night):** Strip beds the morning of move day. Bag mattresses. Pack one set of sheets, pillows, and a blanket into the **Open First box**.
- [ ] Disassemble bed frames. **Hardware in a labeled zip bag taped to the headboard.**
- [ ] **Declutter:** clothes you haven't worn in a year, worn-out shoes, extra hangers.

---

### 11. 🐶 DOG GEAR + OPEN FIRST BOX + CAR KIT (Jul 15 · 1–2 hrs · M)

- [ ] Pack the **dog kit** from the one-page moving-day checklist (food, water, bowls, leash, meds, records, bed, toy, calming aids).
- [ ] Pack a **separate dog "arrival box"**: extra food, a second bed or blanket, toys, poop bags, and enzyme cleaner for accidents in the new place.
- [ ] Keep the dog's routine (walks, meal times) as normal as possible during packing week. Dogs pick up on the chaos.
- [ ] Finish the **Open First box** and load it into the car, not the truck.
- [ ] Load the **car kit** and **documents folder**. Do a final check against the printable one-pager.

---

## 🔧 QUICK-REFERENCE: GARAGE + STORAGE UNIT

**🏬 Storage Unit (by Jun 14)**
- [ ] Give move-out notice (check the 10–30 day requirement)
- [ ] Sort on-site: Keep / Sell / Donate / Trash
- [ ] Move keepers to the garage or spare room
- [ ] Check for heat, moisture, or mildew damage
- [ ] Sweep out, remove your lock, get **written move-out confirmation**
- [ ] Cancel autopay and confirm the deposit refund

**🔧 Garage / Shed / Attic (Jun 20–28)**
- [ ] Dispose of hazmat: gas, propane, paint, solvents, aerosols, chemicals (**county hazardous waste drop-off**)
- [ ] **Drain gas and oil** from mowers and power tools
- [ ] **Don't move firewood** (invasive pest risk)
- [ ] Check Oregon plant/soil quarantine rules before bringing plants
- [ ] Sell or donate duplicates and bulky items you won't need
- [ ] Clean and dry bikes, coolers, outdoor gear
- [ ] Bundle long-handled tools. Small tools go in small heavy-duty boxes
- [ ] Set aside a **car toolkit** (drill, screwdrivers, Allen keys, tape measure, utility knife, hammer)

## 📅 Using .ics Instead of CSV

**Why .ics:** It's the universal calendar format, and it can carry **built-in alerts**, which CSV can't.

**How to import:**
- **iPhone/Mac (Apple Calendar):** On a Mac, double-click the `.ics` file, or use **File → Import** and choose a "Move" calendar. On iPhone, open the file from Mail, Messages, or Files and tap **Add All**. **Alerts are kept.**
- **Google Calendar:** Use the same steps as CSV (**Settings → Import & export → Import**). **Google ignores the alerts in the file on import**, so set default notifications on the Move calendar instead.
- **Sharing:** Import once into a shared calendar (Google or iCloud) so you don't both have to import.

**Format:** Each event looks like this. Save the file as `move.ics` (UTF-8):

```
BEGIN:VCALENDAR
VERSION:2.0
PRODID:-//Move Plan//EN
BEGIN:VEVENT
UID:mover-confirm-20260709@moveplan
DTSTAMP:20260507T060000Z
DTSTART;TZID=America/New_York:20260709T090000
DTEND;TZID=America/New_York:20260709T093000
SUMMARY:⭐ Mover confirmation
DESCRIPTION:Arrival window, crew size, payment, final estimate, parking/elevator access (J)
BEGIN:VALARM
TRIGGER:-PT30M
ACTION:DISPLAY
DESCRIPTION:Reminder
END:VALARM
END:VEVENT
END:VCALENDAR
```

To add more events, repeat everything from `BEGIN:VEVENT` to `END:VEVENT` with a **unique UID** for each. The `TRIGGER:-PT30M` line sets a 30-minute-before alert. Change it to `-PT1H` (1 hour) or `-P1D` (1 day) as you like.

I can generate the **complete `.ics` file with all 38 events and alerts** if you'd prefer that over CSV.
